title_ar: الشيخ الددو: يُشرع في أيام العشر الاهتمام بشأن المسلمين
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew: Concern for the Affairs of the Muslims Is Called For in the Ten Days
body_ar:
قال فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو إنه مما يشرع في هذه الأيام العشر الاهتمام بشأن المسلمين والسعي لتخفيف الظلم عن المظلومين منهم، فأمتنا الإسلامية كالجسد الواحد إذا اشتكى منه عضو تداعى له سائر الجسد بالحمى والسهر.

فحال المسلمين اليوم في مصر والشام وغزة المحاصرة، وفي العراق وبنكلاديش وفي بورما وغيرها يستحق الاهتمام.

وقال الددو في كلمة له بمناسبة عشر ذي الحجة إن حال الأمة اليوم يستحق من المسلمين أن يشعروا به ويهتموا لما أصاب أمتهم ويسعوا للتخفيف من معاناة إخوانهم في بلاد الإسلام.

مؤكدا أنه يجب على الأمة في مثل هذه الظروف أن تقف مع الحق وأن تنصر المظلوم فذلك من الفرائض المتعينة.

وعدد فضيلة الشيخ جملة من الطاعات والأعمال الصالحة التي تُشرع في عشر ذي الحجة، مثل صيامها وبخاصة يوم عرفة؛ الذي هو أفضل أيام السنة.

كذلك يشرع في الأيام التحميد والتكبير والتهليل؛ إضافة إلى التهيئة للعيد.

يمكن مشاهدة كلمة الشيخ الددو من خلال الرابط التالي:

http://dedewnet.com/index.php/search.html?view=media&id=1962
body_en:
His eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew said that among the things called for in the Sharia (yushraʿ) in these ten days is concern for the affairs of the Muslims and striving to lighten the oppression borne by those among them who are wronged; for our Islamic Ummah is like a single body — when one limb of it complains, the rest of the body is summoned to it in fever and sleeplessness.

The condition of the Muslims today in Egypt, in Syria (al-Shām), in besieged Gaza, in Iraq, in Bangladesh, in Burma and elsewhere deserves such concern.

Al-Dedew said, in an address he gave on the occasion of the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah, that the state of the Ummah today deserves that the Muslims should feel it, should be concerned at what has befallen their Ummah, and should strive to lighten the suffering of their brothers in the lands of Islam.

He affirmed that it is obligatory (wājib) upon the Ummah in circumstances such as these to stand with the truth and to support the one who is wronged, for that is among the obligations that devolve upon them specifically (al-farāʾiḍ al-mutaʿayyinah).

His eminence the Sheikh enumerated a number of acts of obedience and righteous deeds that are called for in the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah, such as fasting them, and in particular the day of ʿArafah, which is the best of the days of the year.

Likewise, what is called for in these days is the praise of God, the magnification of Him and the declaration of His oneness — in addition to preparing for the Eid.

Sheikh al-Dedew's address may be watched at the following link:

http://dedewnet.com/index.php/search.html?view=media&id=1962

flags.arabic: صيغة الخبر الصحفي (قال فضيلة الشيخ... مؤكدا... وأضاف...)
options: render as a site news report, with the Sheikh's words marked as the site's paraphrase
render as a text by the Sheikh
flags.note: NOT A TEXT BY THE SHEIKH. This record is the site's own news write-up. Outside the passages placed in quotation marks, every formulation is the site editor's indirect report of what the Sheikh said, not his own wording, and the English preserves the reporting verbs (the Sheikh said that..., he affirmed that...) so that a reader can see this. It must not be displayed as a fatwa or as a text of his. The underlying address or lecture is not in this record.

flags.context: the report of the Sheikh's words on standing with the truth and supporting the wronged
options: among the obligations that devolve upon them specifically (al-farāʾiḍ al-mutaʿayyinah)
among the obligations that have become individually binding (equivalent to farḍ ʿayn here)
among the obligations that are determined and unavoidable
flags.note: farīḍah mutaʿayyinah is not in the glossary. In Maliki usage mutaʿayyin normally marks an obligation that has narrowed onto a particular person or body because no one else will discharge it, which is close to but not simply identical with farḍ ʿayn (glossary: 'individually obligatory'). Rendering it flatly as farḍ ʿayn would put a technical classification in the Sheikh's mouth that the Arabic here does not quite make, and this is a reporter's summary of his words, not his own text. Left literal, with the Arabic, and flagged.

flags.arabic: كالجسد الواحد إذا اشتكى منه عضو تداعى له سائر الجسد بالحمى والسهر
options: translate as the reporter's own words, as printed
mark it as a quotation of the prophetic report
flags.note: This is the wording of a well-known prophetic report (in Muslim, on the mutual mercy of the believers), but the site prints it unattributed and unmarked, running on from the reporter's sentence. Style guide section 4 requires an attribution to be preserved exactly as given; here none is given, so none has been added. Translated as it stands and flagged.

flags.context: the CMS timestamp on the record
options: treat as the date the item was uploaded to the CMS
treat as the date of composition
flags.note: CORPUS-WIDE DEFECT. The CMS serves a bulk-upload timestamp, not the date the Sheikh spoke or wrote. date_is_cms_upload is set true. Where the body itself names a date, that internal date is the better evidence and is kept in the English.

translator_notes: يشرع / تُشرع is the passive 'is legislated, is called for in the Sharia'. It is deliberately weaker than a ruling word and has NOT been mapped onto the five rulings; only the explicit يجب has been rendered 'obligatory (wājib)'.

الشام is rendered 'Syria (al-Shām)'. The Arabic term is wider than the modern state, but the list it sits in (Egypt, Gaza, Iraq, Bangladesh, Burma) is a list of contemporary states and the 2013 context is the Syrian war.
The closing link is to the site's own media system; the address itself is audio or video and is not in this record.
